title: kv cache: improve eviction, spillover and defrag heuristics to reduce fragmentation and OOMs
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Production inference fleets have been seeing sporadic OOMs and increased latency tail under high prefix-KV reuse workloads. Root cause analysis showed cache fragmentation (many small allocations), aggressive paging/spillover causing extra io and latency, and eviction heuristics that didn't prioritize defragmentation-friendly candidates. This PR updates the KV cache allocator, eviction scoring, and spillover policy to reduce fragmentation, limit unnecessary paging, and prefer defragmentation targets when reclaiming memory.

Changes in this PR: 1) Introduce a compaction-friendly eviction score that increases priority for adjacent small fragments to encourage coalescing during reclaim. 2) Add an adaptive spillover threshold driven by live fragmentation metrics so we avoid spilling frequently-accessed KV shards. 3) Refactor the KV allocator to preferentially allocate from larger continuous free ranges when safe, reducing future fragmentation. 4) Add new Prometheus metrics: kv_fragmentation_ratio, kv_spill_decisions, kv_defrag_reclaims. 5) Add unit and integration tests and an end-to-end canary run against small and large sequence-length workloads.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in ENG-3221 - [x] Unit tests for allocator and eviction logic - [x] Integration test for spillover path - [x] Benchmarks: microbench + canary run - [x] Metrics + dashboards updated - [x] Backcompat: configs default to previous thresholds

Testing notes: Ran microbenchmarks with representative LLM decoding traces: observed a 28% reduction in allocation churn and 3% median token latency improvement at 99th percentile tail reduced by ~6%. Canary on dedicated cluster eliminated repeat OOMs seen during prior stress tests. CI initially had a flake in a scheduler test; reran and passed.

Notes: This keeps default behavior unchanged unless fragmentation metrics exceed thresholds; operators can tune kv.defrag.enabled and kv.spill.threshold in runtime config. See release notes for recommended knob values.

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Can you clarify why the allocator prefers larger ranges by default? Concern about contention on large ranges on multi-threaded workloads.

Aisha Patel: We added heuristics to prefer larger ranges only when the request size is > 64KB or when fragmentation ratio > 0.15. Otherwise allocation remains best-fit; added comment and unit test to assert behavior.
Lara Chen: Please add a guard to avoid oscillation between spilling and reclaiming on noisy workloads.
Aisha Patel: Added hysteresis to spill thresholds and a cooldown window; documented choice in comments and runtime config.
Omar Haddad: Can we add a short-term gauge for number of contiguous coalesces per minute? Would help ops debug.
Aisha Patel: Added kv_defrag_reclaims metric; will add dashboard tile as follow-up (small change).

perf-bench: pass (3% median latency improvement, 28% allocation churn reduction)

release_notes: Improve KV cache memory management: adaptive spillover thresholds, defrag-aware eviction scoring, and allocator tweaks to reduce fragmentation and OOMs. Backward compatible; operators can tune kv.defrag.* and kv.spill.* knobs.
notes_for_cherry_pick: No runtime config schema changes; safe to cherry-pick to release branches with the canary config enabled. See docs/operational/kv_cache.md for knobs.
